The error named is a method (reacting to every miss), not a person; 'The agent got this wrong' framing stays on the agent and 'One wrong line in one digest is worth a note' is explicitly not a failure. No shame wording.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L5 header 'A list of don'ts does not teach good work' names a negative case, but the body turns to the positive form ('Every quote names the interview it came from, like this one') and the slide's slug is show-what-good-looks-like; the two other headers lead with the discipline (writing down, recurrence). 'don'ts' is not a failure word of the fabrication/violation kind.

Facets: front-run - L3 slide names 'a rule, a check or an example of good' as plain words, with no Day 3 'what good means is yours to write' framing or slicing pre-empted; arc - closes Day 2 on transfer (squint: after 'Each of you makes something'), Day 3 opens on 'Slice by what you learn' with no bridge in the lecture; Big Idea - 'you were right all along, and now it is dangerous' is honoured by making the team's knowledge the lever ('Finding it is the work'); mood doesn't resolve early - the Day 2 unease is turned into a habit, which is the closer's job, and the stance question is not answered here.
